Test the Markov Order of Sequence Data

Source: R/markov_order.R
markov_order.Rd

Tests whether the sequences of a model are described by a Markov chain of order one, the assumption of a transition network, or whether the next state also depends on states further back.

Usage

markov_order(x, max_order = 3L, iter = 1000L, level = 0.05, dof = "paths")

# S3 method for class 'tna'
markov_order(x, max_order = 3L, iter = 1000L, level = 0.05, dof = "paths")

# S3 method for class 'group_tna'
markov_order(x, max_order = 3L, iter = 1000L, level = 0.05, dof = "paths")

Arguments

x

A tna or a group_tna object created from sequence data.

max_order

An integer, the highest order to test. The default is 3. A value that is not lower than the length of the longest sequence is reduced to that length minus one, with a message.

iter

An integer, the number of permutations for each order. The default is 1000.

level

A numeric value, the significance level of the tests. The default is 0.05.

dof

A character string, how the parameters of each order are counted for AIC and BIC: "paths" (the default) or "observed". See 'Details'.

Value

A tna_markov_order object, which is a list with the elements:

  • stats: A data.frame with one row per order from 0 to max_order and the columns order, loglik, aic, bic (the multi-order model), g2 (the \(G^2\) statistic), df (its degrees of freedom), p_value (the permutation p-value), p_asymptotic (the \(\chi^2\) p-value), and significant (p_value < level). The test columns are NA for order 0 and for an order whose statistic has no degrees of freedom.

  • selected_order: The order selected by the sequential tests.

  • aic_order, bic_order: The orders that minimize AIC and BIC.

  • null: A list with the permutation distribution of \(G^2\) for each order.

  • states: The states observed in the data.

  • n_sequences, n_observations: The numbers of sequences (after splitting at missing values) and states used.

  • max_order, iter, level, dof: The settings used.

For a group_tna object, a group_tna_markov_order object, which is a list of tna_markov_order objects, one per group.

Details

For each order \(k = 1, \ldots,\) max_order, the test compares order \(k - 1\) (the null hypothesis) with order \(k\). Every window of \(k + 1\) consecutive states is split into the context \(w\) (the \(k - 1\) states before the next state), the state \(x\) that order \(k\) adds (\(k\) steps back), and the next state \(s\). Under the null hypothesis, \(s\) is independent of \(x\) given \(w\). This is tested with the likelihood-ratio statistic $$G^2 = 2 \sum_{w, x, s} N_{wxs} \log \frac{N_{wxs} N_{w}}{N_{wx} N_{ws}}$$ with \(\sum_w (r_w - 1)(c_w - 1)\) degrees of freedom, where \(r_w\) and \(c_w\) are the numbers of distinct states \(x\) and \(s\) observed with context \(w\) (Anderson & Goodman, 1957). For \(k = 1\) the context is empty, and the test is whether the next state depends on the current state at all.

The p-value comes from a conditional permutation test: within each context \(w\), the next states are shuffled, which keeps every count that the null hypothesis conditions on. The windows of a sequence overlap, so the permutation distribution approximates the null distribution but is not exact (an exact test would sample whole sequences with the same counts; Besag & Mondal, 2013). The asymptotic \(\chi^2\) p-value is reported alongside.

The orders are tested in sequence: the order is raised while the test rejects at level level. The selected order is the highest order whose test, and the test of every lower order, rejected. Order 0 means that the next state does not depend on the current state, and max_order means that no test failed to reject.

The results also contain the log-likelihood, AIC, and BIC of the multi-order model of each order (Scholtes, 2017). This model uses the state frequencies for the first state of a sequence and the highest available order for each following state. With dof = "paths", the parameters of an order are all the transitions of the paths that the first-order transitions allow, observed or not (Scholtes, 2017). With dof = "observed", only the transitions observed in the data are counted. The orders that minimize AIC and BIC are reported next to the selected order, but they do not affect the test.

Because the tests stop at the first order that does not reject, a dependence that skips an order (for example, on the state two steps back but not on the current state) is not selected. A warning of class tna_warning_markov_order is therefore raised, and a note is printed, when the test of an order above the selected order plus one rejects, or when AIC or BIC select a different order than the tests. The same class of warning is raised when iter is too small for any p-value to fall below level (fewer than floor(1 / level) permutations).

Sequences are split at missing values, so that no window spans a missing value, and the parts with fewer than two states are not used. The windows are treated as independent observations, so sequences nested in actors (for example, several sessions per student) are not taken into account.

References

Anderson, T. W., & Goodman, L. A. (1957). Statistical inference about Markov chains. The Annals of Mathematical Statistics, 28(1), 89–110. doi:10.1214/aoms/1177707039

Besag, J., & Mondal, D. (2013). Exact goodness-of-fit tests for Markov chains. Biometrics, 69(2), 488–496. doi:10.1111/biom.12009

Scholtes, I. (2017). When is a network a network? Multi-order graphical model selection in pathways and temporal networks. In Proceedings of the 23rd ACM SIGKDD International Conference on Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining (pp. 1037–1046). doi:10.1145/3097983.3098145

Examples

model <- tna(group_regulation)
# Small number of permutations for CRAN
mo <- markov_order(model, max_order = 2, iter = 50)
mo
#> Markov order test (50 permutations per order, 2000 sequences, 27533 states)
#> 
#>  order    loglik       aic       bic       g2  df p_value p_asymptotic
#>      0 -53280.55 106577.10 106642.88                                  
#>      1 -46660.94  93475.87  94109.05 13203.77  64   0.020        0.000
#>      2 -46377.27  94110.53  99685.82   561.07 532   0.275        0.185
#>  significant
#>             
#>          yes
#>           no
#> 
#> Selected order: 1 (sequential permutation tests at level 0.05)
#> Order with the lowest AIC: 1; lowest BIC: 1
summary(mo)
#>  order    loglik       aic       bic       g2  df p_value p_asymptotic
#>      0 -53280.55 106577.10 106642.88                                  
#>      1 -46660.94  93475.87  94109.05 13203.77  64   0.020        0.000
#>      2 -46377.27  94110.53  99685.82   561.07 532   0.275        0.185
#>  significant
#>             
#>          yes
#>           no
plot(mo)

plot(mo, panel = "ic")
